# The global rebar build is 4 days stale, and it SILENTLY disables the LLM tier of plan review

## Context / Problem
This machine's global `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` is supposed to track `origin/main` HOURLY via a
rollback-guarded LaunchAgent (documented in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`). IT HAS NOT RUN
SINCE 2026-07-27 17:10 — measured from the mtime of
`/Users/joeoakhart/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar/lib/python3.14/site-packages/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py`,
and corroborated by the venv directory's own mtime. Today is 2026-07-31, so the global build is ~4
days behind main.

**THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT DEGRADATION OF THE REVIEW GATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT
HOUSEKEEPING.** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries `activate` as a DICT (scoped per review type),
which main's overlay parser accepts — `git show origin/main:src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py | grep
"must be a list of ids"` returns NOTHING. The stale global build predates that: its overlay.py DOES
contain that check and raises `CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. Support
landed in `f3dbe32b0b` (2026-07-27, "3ba4: Scope project criteria by review type") and
`7f4c650114` (2026-07-28).

MEASURED consequence of running `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` with the global build in this repo:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay .../.rebar/criteria_routing.json:
                  'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command EXITS 2 and emits a sidecar. It does not present as a broken install; it presents as a
plan that could not be reviewed. The DET tier still runs and reports pass/fail per criterion, so the
output looks substantive. An operator or agent reading that verdict would reasonably conclude the
TICKET is the problem. **No LLM review happened at all.**

The worktree build parses the same file fine — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 effective
criteria — so this is purely the stale global install, not a repo defect.

## Why this matters beyond one command
AGENTS.md already warns to run the repo checkout's build rather than a stale global install, and gives
the reason as "silently ignores newer config keys". This incident shows the consequence is worse than
ignoring a key: an unrelated-looking INDETERMINATE on the claim gate. Any agent that trusts
`which rebar` gets it. The MCP server is affected the same way and, per the local docs, will not
hot-reload.

## Approach
Two separable pieces:
 1. DIAGNOSE why the LaunchAgent stopped. Check `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
    for its last exit status, and the agent's own log, before forcing a sync. A rollback-guarded updater
    that silently gave up 4 days ago has its own failure to explain — forcing a sync hides the evidence.
    Force it only after capturing that state:
    `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`.
 2. MAKE THE STALENESS LOUD rather than silent. A gate run whose LLM tier dies on a CONFIG-PARSE error
    from the installed build is not the same as an LLM outage, and collapsing both into
    `llm_unavailable` + INDETERMINATE is what made this cost time. A `CriteriaError` while loading the
    overlay is a CONFIGURATION fault: it should surface distinctly (its own verdict reason or a loud
    warning naming the installed build's version), so the reader is pointed at the install rather than
    at the plan.

## Scope
- The LaunchAgent / updater: diagnosis first, then a sync.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — distinguish a config-parse failure from an LLM outage in the verdict's
  `llm_error` / reason surfacing.
- Possibly a startup or gate-time warning when the running build's commit is far behind the repo's.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion below is verifiable IN-SESSION by a probe, experiment, or test — no criterion defers
to a future change.

ALL OF THEM ARE TAGGED [operator-attested], and that is a statement of fact rather than a way around
the gate: the completion verifier reads REPOSITORY FILES ONLY, while every probe here observes
machine-local operational state — a launchd exit code, a pipx venv's recorded backend, `command -v uv`
under a given PATH, the contents of ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log. NO repository file can record
any of it, because THE FIX ITSELF TOUCHES NO REPOSITORY FILE (it is one line of a script under
~/.local/bin plus recreating a venv). The observed outputs are pasted verbatim in the evidence comment
on this ticket so the attestation is checkable rather than merely asserted. The code hardening that was previously bundled here (reporting an overlay
`CriteriaError` distinctly from an LLM outage, and naming the installed build as the suspect) has been
SPLIT OUT to its own ticket, because it is a repo change with its own review and must not hold this
environment repair open.

- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE A, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: `~/.local/bin/uv` (0.7.18) shadowed `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`
      (0.12.0) on the updater's PATH. Probe: under the script's ORIGINAL PATH order,
      `command -v uv` resolves the 0.7.18 binary; under the fixed order it resolves 0.12.0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE B, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: the pipx venv was pinned to the pip backend, which pipx
      will not override. Probe: `pipx_metadata.json` recorded `backend = pip` before and records
      `backend = uv` after; and `pipx install --force --backend uv` against the OLD venv was
      demonstrably IGNORED (same `resolution-too-deep`, metadata unchanged).
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE UPDATER COMPLETES: a run exits 0 and `last-good.sha` advances off the Jul-17 commit
      (`4dd9172b9`) to the current tip of `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IT WORKS UNDER LAUNCHD, NOT JUST BY HAND: `launchctl kickstart -k` the agent and then
      `launchctl print` reports `last exit code = 0`. This is the criterion that matters — every
      by-hand run inherits the operator's rich shell environment, whereas launchd supplies a minimal
      one, so a by-hand pass does not prove the scheduled job works.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE INSTALL PATH ITSELF IS EXERCISED UNDER LAUNCHD, not just the no-op branch: with
      `last-good.sha` temporarily rewound, a launchd-triggered run performs a real install and
      advances it again (restore the true sha afterwards). Without this, a green kickstart only
      proves the `no change` early-exit.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IDEMPOTENCE: an immediately following run is a no-op — it logs `no change (already on <sha>)`
      and exits 0 rather than reinstalling.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE MUTATION BITES: restoring the original PATH order reproduces the exact
      `pipx needs uv>=0.9.17` failure, proving the one-line fix is load-bearing and not incidental.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS GONE: the GLOBAL build parses the dict-shaped `activate` in
      `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns the full criteria
      set where it previously raised `CriteriaError`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE GATE ACTUALLY RUNS ON THE GLOBAL BUILD: a real `rebar review-plan` invoked with the GLOBAL
      build reaches the LLM tier (`llm_ran: true`), not merely a successful criteria parse. This is
      the end-to-end form of the reported failure, whose signature was `llm_ran: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE SMOKE-TEST/ROLLBACK GUARD IS INTACT: the script's post-install smoke test still gates
      `last-good.sha`, evidenced by the smoke commands exiting 0 against the freshly installed build.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE KNOWLEDGE IS RECORDED where the next person will look: the local runbook documents that
      PATH order is load-bearing, that `uv` is a hard requirement (so `--backend pip` is NOT a valid
      workaround for this package), that an existing venv pins its backend, and that `update.log` —
      not the 0-byte launchd logs — is the diagnostic file.
